thread:
anya: Quick sync — I'm about to merge a migration PR that standardizes a few terms across the site. Heads-up for SDK owners, examples will change. :eyes:
mike: which terms exactly? can you paste the list?
anya: Main ones: `model_version` -> `model_release`, 'dedicated capacity' -> 'Dedicated', and 'fallback model' -> 'model variant (fallback)'. Also normalizing 'RLHF' -> 'reinforcement learning from human feedback' on first mention.
priya: thanks. I saw a couple of tutorials still use `model_version` in the code snippets. Which PR is this?
anya: <https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/789|#789> — summary in the PR description.
mike: ok i'll update the SDK snippets. There are three spots in the Python quickstart that use `model_version` in the call: `client.generate(model_version="v1")` -> new arg name is `model_release`. does that break compatibility?
priya: good question. We decided (in the SDK council) to keep a thin shim: the SDK will accept `model_release` and `model_version` for one release, but docs should show `model_release`. I'll add a migration note.
sam: I'll run a grep across the docs site for both terms and push a small fix branch if I find leftovers. quick note: watch for lowercase/titlecase differences — search for "Model Version", "model version", etc.
anya: perfect. Also there's a UX copy alignment: product prefers title case for product names, so use "Dedicated" (capital D) when referring to our product offering, and lowercase "dedicated" only for generic use. Priya, can you add that to the style guide's naming table?
priya: putting it in now. I'll add a row: term: Dedicated | canonical: Dedicated | alt forms: dedicated capacity, dedicated GPU pool (note: only lowercase when generically describing capacity).
mike: small snippet I'll change in Python quickstart:
```
# old
resp = client.generate(model_version="v1", prompt="Hello")
# new
resp = client.generate(model_release="v1", prompt="Hello")
```
I'll open the PR against docs and link it to the migration note.
anya: sweet. docs-bot, can you run the link-checker in this thread once PRs land?
docs-bot: running link-check for PRs referenced: #789, #795. Report will be posted in ~10m.
sam: FYI I found 4 remaining mentions in the examples folder, two in /examples/embeddings/ and two in /examples/chat/. I'll push a fix branch and reference this thread.
priya: when you push, please include a short migration blurb in each example README: "Old param `model_version` renamed to `model_release` — SDKs accept both during transition."
mike: will do. Also adding a tiny note for downstream integrators: param names changed but behavior identical.
anya: action items: mike — update SDK snippets and open PR linking to #789; sam — push fixes to examples and run grep for casing; priya — add canonicalization table row + migration blurb; docs-bot — run link-check and report. Merge target end of day Thursday.
priya: one more: can we standardize on 'model variant' for fallback language? I got a PM asking to avoid the word 'fallback' as it sounds negative.
anya: yes — use "model variant (fallback)" first time, then "model variant" thereafter. I'll add that to the style sheet.
mike: PR opened: <https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/795|#795> with the Python and JS snippet updates.
docs-bot: link-check complete: no broken links in #789 or #795. Found 1 anchor mismatch in /docs/guides/migration.md — filing an issue. <https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/310|#310>.
sam: awesome, i'll patch the anchor in my examples PR.
anya: thanks team. if nobody objects i'll merge the canonicalization PR after the example fixes land to avoid churn. :+1:
priya: no objections from me.
mike: good to go from SDK side.
sam: merging fixes this afternoon.
anya: closing thread once merged. Thanks all!
